caveats: Comes from GLDAS Noah, a computer model of the land surface driven by observations; it is not measured directly.
Land only, between 60 degrees south and the North Pole; there are no values over the ocean or Antarctica.
Each value is an average over a 2 x 2 degree cell (about 220 km wide); cells that are mostly ocean are left out.
variables.definition: How much water moves from the land into the air, by evaporating from soil and water and by plants releasing it through their leaves, as an average amount per day.
variables.increase_means: An increase means more water went from the land into the air.
variables.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)

caveats: Comes from GPM IMERG, an estimate from satellites combined with rain gauges, not a direct measurement everywhere.
The satellites that feed IMERG changed during the record, which can affect long-term trends.
Each value is an average over a 2 x 2 degree cell (about 220 km wide).
variables.definition: How much water falls from the sky as rain or snow, given as the average amount per day in each month.
variables.increase_means: An increase means more rain or snow fell on average.
variables.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)

caveats: Comes from GLDAS Noah, a computer model of the land surface driven by observations; it is not measured directly.
Land only, between 60 degrees south and the North Pole.
Surface runoff happens in short bursts after heavy rain or snowmelt, so monthly values are small in many places.
variables.definition: Rain or melted snow that flows over the ground instead of soaking into the soil, as an average amount per day.
variables.increase_means: An increase means more water ran off over the ground surface.
variables.name: Water running off the surface

caveats: Comes from GLDAS Noah, a computer model of the land surface driven by observations; it is not measured directly.
1 kg/m² of water is the same as a layer of water 1 mm deep.
Only the top 10 cm of soil; deeper soil can change differently.
Land only, between 60 degrees south and the North Pole.
variables.definition: How much water is held in the top 10 centimeters of soil.
variables.increase_means: An increase means the topsoil got wetter.
variables.long_name: soil moisture content in the 0-10 cm layer, monthly mean
variables.name: Water in the topsoil

caveats: Comes from MERRA-2, a reanalysis (a weather model combined with many observations), not from a thermometer in every place.
Each value is an average over a 2 x 2 degree cell (about 220 km wide), so local differences such as a single city are not visible.
variables.definition: How warm the air is about 2 meters above the ground or the sea, averaged over each month.
variables.increase_means: An increase means the air near the surface got warmer.
variables.name: Air temperature near the ground
